title: Method Bugs & Output Prediction
summary: Analyze common interview bugs: missing return statement on conditional paths, unreachable code, and variable shadowing.
learningOutcomes: Diagnose compiler errors related to return contracts
Predict output of multi-method interaction chains accurately
Identify and fix variable shadowing pitfalls

activities.title: Core Mechanics: Method Bugs & Output Prediction

breakdown.whatIsIt: Comprehensive exploration of Method Bugs & Output Prediction in Java.
breakdown.whyItMatters: Crucial for writing maintainable, reusable, and bug-free Java applications.
howItWorks: Decomposes complex logic into self-contained subprograms.
Allocates local variables on Call Stack frames.
Passes arguments by value, copying parameter data into frames.
Returns execution control back to caller upon reaching return statement.
keyTakeaways: Mastering Method Bugs & Output Prediction is essential for Java placement interviews and clean architecture.
Methods enforce the DRY principle by eliminating redundant duplicate code.
Parameters act as local placeholders; arguments provide runtime values.
Always consider edge cases such as invalid input parameters or stack overflow.

activities.title: Verified Java Implementation: Method Bugs & Output Prediction
activities.description: Trace step-by-step how variable scope, return statements, and call sequencing determine exact output.

questions.prompt: What error does the compiler produce for: 'int f(int x) { if (x > 0) return 1; }'?
options: Variable x might not have been initialized
questions.explanation: If x <= 0, no return statement is executed. Java requires guaranteed returns on all execution paths.

questions.prompt: Why does 'public static int test() { return 5; System.out.println("Hi"); }' fail to compile?
questions.explanation: Placing any code immediately after an unconditional return statement results in an unreachable code error.

questions.prompt: Given: 'static int val = 50; static void setVal(int val) { val = 100; }'. If we call setVal(20), what is class variable val afterwards?
questions.explanation: The parameter 'val' shadows the static class field 'val'. 'val = 100' only alters the local parameter copy. The static class field remains 50.

questions.prompt: Given: 'int a = 2; doWork(a, ++a);'. In what order are arguments evaluated?
options: Strictly from left to right: first arg is 2, then ++a increments a to 3, passing 3 as second arg
Randomly based on OS thread scheduling
questions.explanation: Java strictly evaluates method arguments from left to right. The first argument evaluates to 2, and the second evaluates to 3.

questions.prompt: What is the output of the following: 'int x = 10; test(x); System.out.println(x);' where 'void test(int x) { x = x * 2; }'?
questions.explanation: Due to pass-by-value, test() modifies only its local parameter copy. The caller's x remains 10.

questions.prompt: How can you explicitly assign a value to a shadowed static class field 'count' inside a method with parameter 'int count'?
questions.explanation: Qualifying the field name with the class name (e.g. MyClass.count = count) bypasses parameter shadowing.

questions.prompt: What happens if a method specifies return type 'void' but contains 'return 10;'?
options: Compiler error: incompatible types: unexpected return value
questions.explanation: A void method cannot return any value. 'return 10;' causes a compile error.

questions.prompt: Is 'if (true) return 1; else return 2;' considered missing a return statement by the compiler?
options: No, both if and else paths guarantee a return statement
Only on older versions of Java
questions.explanation: Because both the 'if' branch and the 'else' branch return a value, all execution paths are covered.

practice.title: Fix Missing Return Statement
practice.problemStatement: Fix the flawed method 'describeSign(int n)' so that it returns 'Positive' for n > 0, 'Negative' for n < 0, and 'Zero' for n == 0. In main(), test with 5, -3, and 0.

5 is Positive

interviewQA.question: Why does the Java compiler enforce definite return analysis on all conditional branches?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Java enforces strict type and memory safety. If a method declaring a non-void return type were allowed to reach the end of its body without returning a value, the caller would receive undefined memory or crash. The compiler verifies that every execution path terminates with an appropriate return statement.
keyPoints: Focus on memory lifecycle and compile-time contract enforcement.

interviewQA.question: What is variable shadowing and how is it different from variable hiding?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Variable shadowing occurs when a local variable or parameter shares the same name as an instance or static variable in the enclosing class scope, hiding it from direct unqualified access. Variable hiding occurs in inheritance when a subclass declares a field or static method with the same name as a superclass field or static method.
keyPoints: Focus on memory lifecycle and compile-time contract enforcement.

interviewQA.question: Why does Java treat unreachable code as a compile-time error instead of a warning?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: The Java Language Specification (JLS §14.21) explicitly requires that every statement in a program be reachable. Treating unreachable code as an error prevents dead logic, copy-paste errors, and misunderstandings about program flow before code can enter production.
keyPoints: Focus on memory lifecycle and compile-time contract enforcement.

interviewQA.question: What is the result of 'return;' in a void method versus a non-void method?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: In a void method, 'return;' is valid and immediately halts execution, returning control to the caller. In a non-void method, 'return;' without an expression causes a compile-time error: 'missing return value'.
keyPoints: Focus on memory lifecycle and compile-time contract enforcement.

interviewQA.question: How does Java handle argument evaluation when one argument throws an exception?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Because arguments are evaluated strictly from left to right, if an earlier argument expression throws an exception, subsequent arguments are never evaluated, and the target method is never invoked.
keyPoints: Focus on memory lifecycle and compile-time contract enforcement.

interviewQA.question: Can a method return inside a synchronized block?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Yes. If a return statement executes inside a synchronized block, Java guarantees that the intrinsic monitor lock is automatically released before control returns to the caller.
keyPoints: Focus on memory lifecycle and compile-time contract enforcement.

interviewQA.question: What is the difference between an early return and an exception throw?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: An early return cleanly terminates the method and delivers an expected outcome to the caller. An exception indicates an abnormal, unexpected error condition that disrupts normal flow and unwinds the stack until caught by a matching catch block.
keyPoints: Focus on memory lifecycle and compile-time contract enforcement.

activities.title: Self-Mastery Checklist
checklist: Definite Return: Every single path through a non-void method must return a value; missing a path causes a compile error.
Unreachable Code: Statements directly following unconditional returns or breaks cause compiler errors.
Variable Shadowing: Parameters hide class fields of the same name; qualify with ClassName to access static fields.
Left-to-Right Evaluation: Arguments are evaluated strictly from left to right before method invocation.
Defensive Base Cases: Recursive methods should handle negative or edge inputs to prevent runaway stack overflow.

practiceProblems.title: Detecting Infinite Recursion Edge Case
practiceProblems.description: Write a safe recursive method 'countdownSafe(int n)' that prints n. If n <= 0, print 'Stop'. If n < -10, return immediately to guard against bad negative inputs. In main(), test with 3 and -5.
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Write a safe recursive method 'countdownSafe(int n)' that prints n. If n <= 0, print 'Stop'. If n < -10, return immediately to guard against bad negative inputs. In main(), test with 3 and -5.
practiceProblems.hint: Ensure negative inputs do not recurse indefinitely.
hints: Check n <= 0: print Stop and return.
Otherwise print n and recurse on n - 1.
